description: Automatically control Philips Hue lights based on media playback. Supports multi-profile configuration, scene activation, brightness control, transition duration, media type filtering, and IntroSkipper outro detection.
name: Hue Lighting Control
overview: Control Philips Hue lights based on Jellyfin playback events

versions.changelog:
## Hue API v2

The plugin now speaks Hue's CLIP v2 API exclusively, over HTTPS with the bridge's certificate
verified against Signify's root CA.

**Breaking changes**
- Bridges running software older than 1948086000, and the round v1 bridge, are no longer
  supported. Update the bridge in the Hue app.
- A scene now always lights the room or zone it belongs to. Previously a scene could be
  pointed at the profile's Target Light Group; if you relied on that, choose a scene that
  belongs to the room you want.
- Brightness is a percentage (0–100). Existing profiles are converted once on first start.
- `POST /api/hueplugin/test` takes `{ "Action": "Play" | "Pause" | "Stop", "Profile": { … } }` and answers `{ "Success", "Error" }`; the old `GroupId` / `SceneId` / `Brightness` / `TurnOff` body is rejected.

**Upgrading**
- Stored room and scene ids are rewritten to v2 ids the first time you open the plugin page.
  Anything that no longer exists on the bridge is shown as *Unresolved* and needs re-selecting.
- 4.0 is the only version that converts 3.x settings; upgrade through 4.0 before moving to a later release.

**New**
- Local bridge discovery over mDNS, with Philips' cloud lookup as fallback (SSDP is gone;
  Philips switched it off in 2022).
- The plugin page shows each bridge's id, model and software version, and groups rooms and
  zones in the target dropdown.
- Turning lights off with a transition now fades in one command instead of dim-wait-off.
- A stop event for a previous item can no longer undo the lights for the item that is playing.
- Each Play, Pause and Stop section of the profile editor has its own **Test** button that runs that action with the values on screen, including scenes and transitions, before you save. The profile menu offers Test Play, Test Pause and Test Stop.
- The plugin now uses Jellyfin's service registration and hosted-service lifecycle; the playback listener starts and stops with the server.

**Fixed**
- The API key is no longer sent in the URL, written to the log at any level, or printed to the browser console.
- Editing a bridge's address or key on the plugin page now clears its certificate pin and cached rooms, so the next authentication re-pins instead of every request failing on a subject mismatch.
- The plugin page shows a change only after it is saved. A failed save keeps the editor open with your values and says why, and changes made in quick succession are saved in order.
- Nothing can be saved before the plugin page has finished loading; a failed load offers Retry instead of an empty page that could overwrite your settings.
- Dropping text or anything else that is not a profile card onto a profile no longer deletes a profile. A configuration already damaged this way loads again after the server restarts; the profile that was removed has to be added again.
- Opening a profile whose bridge cannot list its rooms and scenes keeps the profile's own room, scenes and bridge instead of showing another profile's, and says the lists could not be loaded.
- Cancelling Add Bridge stops pairing.
- Transition durations are limited to 15 seconds.
- With two or more bridges, the profile editor asks which bridge a profile uses instead of saving a profile that matches no bridge.
- Blank brightness, transition and grace-period fields block Save and Test with a message naming the field, and typed values are limited to the slider ranges.
- Delete Bridge also refuses while profiles with no bridge chosen depend on it.
- A bridge's connection status can no longer appear on another bridge's card.

## Action required after updating

Open each profile once and re-enter your transition durations. A bug in earlier versions (see below) has already reset them to 0 in existing configurations, and the old values cannot be recovered.

## Fixes

- **Transition durations no longer reset when saving the configuration page.** Any save from the page (adding or re-pairing a bridge, reordering profiles, or editing a different profile) silently set every other profile's transition durations to 0 and switched all three "Custom Transition Duration" options on.
- **Brightness transitions now reach the bridge.** The transition time was sent under a key the Hue bridge rejects, so brightness changes on play, pause and stop used the bridge's default 0.4 s fade regardless of the configured duration. Scene transitions were not affected.
- **Bridge errors are no longer reported as success.** The bridge answers light commands with a per-parameter result inside an HTTP 200 response. A rejected parameter, a revoked API key or an unknown group or scene id is now logged as a `Bridge error for ...` warning, and the Test button reports it as a failure.
- **Re-adding a bridge that already exists no longer creates a duplicate entry.** Both the pairing path and the paste-an-API-key path update the existing bridge, keeping its name and the profiles linked to it. If you already have duplicates, delete the extra entries and keep the one your profiles use.
- **Clearing a transition duration field no longer breaks saving the profile.** An empty field is saved as 0.

## Security

- **The plugin API now requires an administrator account.** Previously any signed-in Jellyfin user could add or delete bridges, obtain the bridge API key by triggering pairing, control lights, and make the server connect to arbitrary hosts through the connection test. The configuration page is unaffected; it already required an administrator.

## Device picker for profile filters

Profiles can now target devices by picking them from a list instead of hunting for Device IDs in the server log. "Add Device ID" in the profile editor's Filters tab shows every device that has signed in to your server, labelled with its name, app, the IP it is currently connected from, the last user, and when it was last seen. Devices already in the profile are hidden, manual entry remains available underneath, and saved IDs are shown with their resolved device name.

Remember that each app and each browser on the same physical device has its own ID, so add every one that should trigger the profile.

## Fixes

- Cancelling a profile edit no longer drops device IDs you removed during the edit.
- Bridge names, profile names, and filter values are HTML-escaped when rendered in the config page.
- Duplicate device ID checks are case-insensitive, matching the server-side filter.

## Housekeeping

- The plugin repository manifest now advertises the correct minimum Jellyfin version for every past release: v1.3.0.0 through v2.2.0.0 require 10.11, v1.2.0.0 and earlier run on 10.9 and 10.10.
- CI moved to current GitHub action majors and pins the .NET 10 SDK band.

Requires **Jellyfin 12.0+**. Jellyfin 10.11 users stay on v2.2.0.0.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ericecook/JellyfinHuePlugin/compare/v3.0.0.0...v3.1.0.0

## Jellyfin 12.0 support

This release targets **Jellyfin 12.0+** (.NET 10). Plugins built for Jellyfin 10.11 do not load on 12.0, so this rebuild is required after upgrading your server.

**Jellyfin 10.11 users:** stay on v2.2.0.0. The plugin catalog will keep offering that version to 10.11 servers and will not offer v3.0.0.0 until you upgrade Jellyfin.

No functional changes to lighting behaviour in this release.


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ericecook/JellyfinHuePlugin/compare/v2.2.0.0...v3.0.0.0

### Multi-Bridge Support
- Support for multiple Hue bridges with independent configuration
- Per-profile bridge assignment — each lighting profile targets a specific bridge
- Bridge CRUD API endpoints for add, edit, and delete
- Automatic migration from single-bridge to multi-bridge configuration

### New Config UI
- Redesigned configuration page with card-based layout
- Profile templates (Movie Theater, TV Viewing, Bedroom Casual, Gaming Setup) for quick setup
- Edit Bridge modal — click any bridge card to modify its name, IP, or API key
- Click-outside-to-close for all modals
- Auto-save on modal save, profile-reorder, etc. (no more global Save button)
- Improved bridge authentication instructions

### Pause Grace Period
- Configurable grace period to skip pause lighting during the first N seconds of playback
- Useful for skipping pause actions while getting settled at the start of a movie

### Bug Fixes & Improvements
- Fixed concurrency bugs in playback session management
- Added comprehensive test coverage
- Fixed long Device IDs overflowing their container
- Replaced IntroSkipper DB hack with Jellyfin Media Segments API (from v1.4.0)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ericecook/JellyfinHuePlugin/compare/v1.4.0.0...v2.0.0.0
